name: University of Leeds

settingEvidence.evidence: Our beautiful and unique single-site campus has got everything you’d find in a small town and is just a short walk from the city centre.

fees.text: £10,050 per year for UK (Home) students starting in 2027/28. Leeds says fees from 2028/29 are likely to rise at least in line with inflation (the government sets the cap). A study abroad or work placement year costs £1,505 for students paying £10,050.

source.evidence: Tuition fees for UK undergraduate students starting in 2027/28 are £10,050.

livingCosts.text: University self-catered accommodation costs about £122–£273 a week (average £198) in 2026/27, with bills and gym membership included; catered halls average £248 a week (£213–£283, 12 meals a week). Leeds estimates total living costs (rent plus food, bills and personal costs, excluding tuition fees) at about £6,670–£18,170 for a 39-week year, average £12,480. University rents are still provisional.

source.evidence: mean average £198 (£122 to £273)

openDays.text: Leeds' 2026 undergraduate open days have finished and 2027 dates are not announced yet. You can book a campus tour in the meantime.

source.evidence: Our 2026 Open Days have now finished, but there are still plenty of ways to explore studying at Leeds.

contextual.summary: Leeds' Access to Leeds scheme gives UK applicants who meet at least two of its criteria an offer up to two grades lower than the standard offer (for example ABB instead of AAA) if they also pass its module, and applicants from Low Participation Neighbourhoods may get one grade off automatically.
contextual.typicalReduction: Access to Leeds: up to two grades lower than the standard offer (for example AAA becomes ABB). Low Participation Neighbourhoods: usually one A-level grade lower.

criteria.detail: Your parents or carers did not go to university: they have not completed an undergraduate degree at a university or polytechnic in the UK or overseas. You also count if they started but did not finish a degree, hold an HNC or HND, an Open University or similar distance-learning degree, a part-time work-based degree, or a degree but you are estranged from them with little or no contact.

Your permanent home postcode (as on your UCAS application) is in an area with low levels of participation in higher education and/or high levels of socioeconomic deprivation, measured against government data. Leeds does not name the dataset on this page.

Household income of £25,000 or below, or you were eligible for free school meals at any point during secondary school (also shown by receiving the 16-19 Bursary Fund or Learner Support because your income is £25,000 or below, or by a parent or carer income declaration). Together these count as one criterion.

You attended or attend a school that performed below the national average at GCSE (its Attainment 8 score compared with the England average). Independent fee-paying schools are not eligible under this criterion.

Your personal circumstances have had a disruptive impact on your education, for example caring responsibilities or being a young carer, a recent close family bereavement, estrangement from your parents or carers, a mental or physical health condition or disability, being from a military service family, or refugee or asylum seeker status. Several instances count as one criterion.

You are a care leaver or have experienced time in care: any time in local authority or formal kinship care, adopted from care, or on a child protection plan after age 11. Care leavers (at least 13 weeks in local authority care spanning their 16th birthday) also count under the personal circumstances criterion.

contextual.rulesText: Access to Leeds: you must meet at least two separate criteria from the personal circumstances list, and also meet all the applicant requirements (UK applicant applying through UCAS to a full-time undergraduate course, holding or studying the required level 3 qualifications, no existing undergraduate degree, not taking a foundation course, no Access to HE Diploma except for Healthcare degrees). Leeds must be your firm choice and you need to pass the Access to Leeds module. Separately, if you live in a Low Participation Neighbourhood (assessed with the Indices of Multiple Deprivation), your offer could be reduced by one A-level grade in most cases; you do not apply separately.

programmes.name: Access to Leeds
programmes.summary: Leeds' contextual admissions programme: meet at least two of its criteria and you can get an offer up to two grades lower than the standard offer (for example ABB instead of AAA), plus a study module and support.
programmes.whoCanApply: UK applicants applying through UCAS to a full-time undergraduate course at Leeds who meet at least two of the six personal circumstances criteria (parents or carers did not go to university; low-participation or deprived area; household income of £25,000 or below or free school meals; school below the national GCSE average; education disrupted by personal circumstances; care experienced) and all the applicant requirements.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Meet at least two separate criteria from the personal circumstances list. You must also live permanently in the UK and be eligible for UK tuition fees, apply via UCAS to a full-time undergraduate course at Leeds, hold or be studying the required level 3 qualifications, not already hold an undergraduate degree, not be taking a foundation course, and not hold or be taking an Access to HE Diploma (except for Healthcare degrees). Leeds needs to be your firm choice on UCAS.

A study module, support and events to help prepare you for university
On-course support through the Plus Programme
Additional consideration if you apply for a means-tested scholarship

programmes.name: Leeds Futures
programmes.summary: A mostly online outreach programme for Year 12 students who pick a subject strand, with webinars, study-skills sessions, one campus taster day and UCAS support in Year 13.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students applying individually. Priority goes to students whose home postcode is in a low-participation area or who meet one or more Access to Leeds criteria. The page does not say whether other students can apply.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: Priority for places goes to students whose home postcode is in an area with low levels of participation in higher education, and to those who meet one or more Access to Leeds criteria: parents or carers did not go to university; household income of £25,000 or below; attended a school below the national GCSE average; personal circumstances that disrupted education; care experienced. Individual strands may have extra criteria.
benefits: Subject webinars, study-skills sessions and Q&As with current students (Year 12 spring term)
A campus taster day with lectures, workshops, chats with students and a campus tour (Year 12 summer term)
Help with UCAS and personal statements in Year 13, plus an overview of Access to Leeds and the Plus Programme
Free lunch on campus days and a travel bursary for eligible students, subject to funding
programmes.subjects: You choose one strand. Social sciences strands for 2027 are Politics and Sociology; other strands include Environment, English/History, Creative Industries, STEM and Health Sciences. No Economics or Business strand is listed.

runs.text: From the spring term of Year 12 (2027) until you submit your UCAS application in Year 13; campus taster day in the Year 12 summer term (date not announced)

programmes.name: Social Sciences Summer School
programmes.summary: A three-day, two-night residential summer school for Year 12 students to try social sciences subjects, including Business, with lectures, seminars and workshops and a stay in university accommodation.
programmes.whoCanApply: Year 12 students. Priority goes to students who live in an area of low progression to higher education and/or meet 1 or 2 of Leeds' listed criteria.
programmes.eligibilityDetail: All Year 12 students can apply, but priority is given to students who live in an area of low progression to higher education and/or meet 1 or 2 of: parents or carers did not go to university; household income of £25,000 or below; attended a school below the national average Attainment 8 score at GCSE; studies disrupted by personal circumstances; eligible for free school meals during GCSE studies or later; care experienced; estranged from parents or guardians.
benefits: University-level lectures, seminars and workshops on the theme 'Creating Change'
Two nights in university accommodation with social activities run by student ambassadors
Online sessions after the event supporting your UCAS application and move to university
A contribution of up to £100 towards travel costs for eligible students

Leeds is not on UAT-UK's official TMUA list for 2027 entry, and none of these course pages names an admissions test.

Economics, Economics and Finance and Business Economics (Leeds University Business School) ask for AAA in any subject; Economics and Mathematics needs an A in A-level Mathematics. The Politics, Geography and PPE joint courses show AAA; their summary boxes say 'specific subject requirements' but the entry sections list none.

Access to Leeds can lower offers by up to two grades (usually to ABB) if you meet at least two criteria and pass its module; Low Participation Neighbourhood postcodes may get one grade off automatically.

Other Business School degrees (for example Accounting and Finance, Banking and Finance, Business Management) were not recorded. Insight2Uni, a mentoring partnership with the charity With Insight for black-heritage Year 12 students in Yorkshire and the Humber, is not recorded as a Leeds programme.
